items.name: Permit domain — enums, models, safety-range constants
items.description: The vocabulary every other item in this module imports: status enum, type enum, JSA phase enum, worker-role sets per permit type, the safety-range constant, and request/response models for the permit endpoints.
acceptance: EPermitStatus: DRAFT | PENDING | REJECTED | ACTIVE | FIRE_MONITOR | CLOSED | EXPIRED
EPermitType: hot | confined | heights
EJsaPhase: pre | process | post
A single exported SAFETY_RANGES constant encoding LEL=0, O2 19.5-23.5, CO<=50 (confined), wind<=25 (heights), and which readings each type requires
A pure validateReadings(type, readings, outdoorWork) helper returning the list of failing readings — unit tested at the boundaries: 0, 19.4, 19.5, 23.5, 23.6, 50, 50.1, 25, 25.1
Worker-role option sets per type (confined: Entrant/Attendant/Gas Tester; hot: Fire Watcher/Operator/Helper; heights: per design)
Request/response models per model-conventions.md for create/patch/submit/list/detail/close/qr/audit
./init.sh green
items.notes: SAFETY_RANGES is imported by both the zod schema and the inline pass/fail UI. Never duplicate the numbers. Ranges are in docs/modules/permit/context.md and AGENTS.md. || DONE. validateReadings(type, readings, outdoorWork) returns IReadingFailure[] = {reading, reason: MISSING|OUT_OF_RANGE} — a list, not a boolean, so the UI can name the failing reading. SO2 and height are advisory: never in the failure list. wind is excluded from bypassableByOutdoor, so outdoorWork never skips it. BACKEND CONFIRMATION NEEDED: the fields project and workDescription come from the design wizard step 2, NOT from the permits table column list in 01-backend-elysia-tasks.md.

items.name: Wizard shell — stepper, navigation, draft persistence
items.description: The 6-step container: stepper header, per-step validation gate on Next, Back navigation, and draft persistence to the API. Step bodies land in PMT-005..009.
acceptance: 6-node stepper with done / current / upcoming states and connecting rules
Next is blocked while the current step's schema fails; the blocked reason is shown next to the button
Back never validates
Step 6 replaces Next with a green Submit button
Draft state persists via POST /permits then PATCH /permits/:id — not localStorage
Wizard state lives in a page-scoped composable (useWizard), not a Pinia store
Steps stack full-width below md
./init.sh green
items.notes: Design lines 146-165 (stepper) and 417-425 (footer). || DONE. Step registry WIZARD_STEPS: IWizardStepDef[] = {key, labelKey, component, schema} — StepperHeader, WizardFooter and useWizard all derive from it, so filling a step means editing only that step .vue + .schema.ts. useWizard(steps) takes an injectable array so tests can exercise gating (the real placeholder schemas always pass). CREATE-THEN-PATCH RACE solved with a single inflight promise chain: doPersist() reads draftId at execution time, not call time, so a second write queues behind the first and never fires a second create — covered by a deferred-promise test. Nothing POSTs until formData.type is set. goToStep re-validates EVERY prior step, not just an unlocked index — otherwise editing an earlier step back into an invalid state would let the stepper jump past it (invisible today, live from PMT-005). 375px: compact Step X of N + progress bar below sm, full 6-node stepper at sm+. Six step stubs each marked with their follow-up item.

items.name: Wizard step 3 — Safety Checks
items.description: Type-specific gas/wind readings with inline pass/fail against SAFETY_RANGES, the indoor/outdoor bypass toggle, the numbered Yes/No/N/A checklist, and a hard block on Next when a reading fails.
acceptance: Readings rendered per type: hot → LEL, O2; confined → LEL, O2, CO, SO2; heights → wind, height-from-ground
Each reading card shows the TH/EN label, the range hint, a mono numeric input with its unit, and an instrument-photo slot
A failing reading turns its card border/background red and blocks Next with NO override; the specific failing reading is named
Blocked banner (#C81E2C) / safe banner (#E4F4EC) above the readings
Indoor/Outdoor toggle sets outdoorWork; outdoor hides the gas readings and shows the bypass info panel; wind for heights is NOT bypassable
Numbered Yes/No/N/A checklist below the readings
Pass/fail comes from the shared validateReadings() from PMT-001 — the numbers are not re-typed here
./init.sh green

items.name: Closure checklist modal
items.description: The foreman-facing closure flow: checklist, e-signature, and honest rendering of both backend block conditions.
acceptance: Checklist rows with ✓ / ✗ buttons; Confirm stays disabled until every row is answered
E-signature pad is revealed only once the checklist is complete; captured signature is stamped with a mono timestamp

FIRE_WATCH_NOT_ELAPSED → closure is blocked with the remaining time

Modal is built on src/components/modal/BaseModal.vue

items.notes: Design lines 574-611. The client must not pre-empt the backend — always attempt the call and render its verdict; the client-side block is only a UX hint.

items.name: Mark-complete + Fire Watch countdown (hot work)
items.description: The hot-work-only path: a confirm dialog explaining the 30-minute server-side countdown, then the orange Fire Monitor panel with a live timer that unlocks closure at zero.
acceptance: ACTIVE hot-work permits show the orange 'Mark Work Complete' strip; confined/heights show the green closure strip instead
Confirm dialog states the countdown is server-side and cannot be bypassed
POST /permits/:id/mark-complete moves the permit to FIRE_MONITOR
Fire Monitor panel: 80px mono MM:SS countdown, progress bar, warning copy, disabled 'Close Permit — locked until MM:SS' button
The countdown is derived from the server's fireMonitorStartedAt, NOT from a client-start timestamp — a page reload must not reset it
At zero, closure unlocks and hands off to PMT-011
./init.sh green
